target_customer: Defense, aerospace and industrial manufacturers needing DFARS-compliant domestic permanent magnets
problem: US magnet supply depends on China; domestic, compliant magnets for motors in robotics and defense are scarce.
business_model: Manufacturer selling permanent magnets made from recycled rare-earth scrap

founders.name: Eric Silver
founders.background_notes: Built pilot cathode lines for lithium-sulfur batteries and materials labs for NSF-funded companies per YC page.

competitors.name: Noveon Magnetics
competitors.what: Texas recycler making magnets from recycled NdFeB via powder metallurgy

competitors.name: Cyclic Materials
competitors.what: Recovers rare earth oxides from end-of-life magnets

technical_complexity.rationale: Sorting scrap by chemistry and rapid sintering to dense magnets that meet performance specs is materials and process engineering with qualification hurdles.

defensibility.rationale: DFARS compliance and process know-how help, but several funded recyclers already operate; process claims are unverified.

market_need_then: Heavy policy and defense focus on US rare-earth supply in 2025 and 2026 and a reported recycling rate of about 1 percent of rare earth magnets globally.

rebrands.why: Not sourced; link between the two names is likely but unconfirmed

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is only a few months old with no press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Mass Magnetics joined YC in Summer 2026 with a three person team and has no public funding or exit, so its outcome cannot yet be assessed. The market tailwind is strong policy attention on domestic rare earth supply, but funded competitors such as Noveon and Cyclic Materials are already ahead on scale.
notes: No funding found. The Greentown member page lists a company named Mass Energy Company (founded 2023) with the same founders; assumed same company but not confirmed. Company website was not fetched directly. Competitors are as of mid 2026, so this record is effectively current.
